stem.text: The number of people waiting in a line, measured in people, is modeled by a twice-differentiable function N of time t, measured in minutes. It is known that \( N''(3) = -3.5 \). Using correct units, interpret the meaning of \( N''(3) = -3.5 \) in the context of the problem.

answer_key.label: At time t = 3 minutes, the rate at which the number of people in the line is changing is decreasing at a rate of 3.5 people per minute per minute.

worked_solution.text: \( N''(3) \) is the rate of change of \( N' \), the rate at which the number of people in the line changes, so it is measured in people per minute per minute.
worked_solution.rule_named: second derivative as the rate of change of a rate

worked_solution.text: The value is negative, so at t = 3 the rate of change of the number of people in the line is itself decreasing, by 3.5 people per minute for each minute.
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of the second derivative gives the direction of change of the rate

options.label: At time t = 3 minutes, the number of people in the line is decreasing at a rate of 3.5 people per minute per minute.
options.derivation: the interpretation speaks of the quantity and leaves out that it is the rate which is changing
